markdown_report:
At 10% progress, prioritize a small **directional recent-history residual**, keeping candidate-set cross-entropy unchanged. Earlier residual attempts scored 0.4037–0.4100 versus the supplied SASRec reference of 0.5050; these results discourage assuming that additional pooling improves validation.

**Insights and directions.** First, the starting idea separates recent evidence from the backbone. Zero initialization permits an initially identical scoring function, but does not guarantee useful subsequent learning. Second, recurrence weighting may emphasize repeated interests. It can also suppress a new interest, so defer it until simpler mechanisms succeed. Third, candidate-set CE makes negative competition explicit. Electronics’ 15.96% sampled negative-win rate motivates investigating separation, without establishing its cause.

From related work, SASRec provides causal context selection. It does not explicitly distinguish directional transitions from symmetric affinity [1]. TiCoSeRec motivates ordered behavioral transitions. A lightweight asymmetric residual tests that principle without constructing its graph [2]. gSASRec motivates objective calibration and additional negatives. Its evidence does not establish superiority over the proposed CE objective [3].

These insights organize three directions: context selection, directional scoring, and objective calibration.

| Framework axis | Existing mechanism | Proposed experiment | Remaining gap |
|---|---|---|---|
| Context | SASRec; recent pooling | Three-event exponential pooling | Recent does not establish current purpose |
| Relations | Tied embedding similarity | Separate source/target projections | Transitions do not establish compatibility |
| Competition | Candidate-set CE; gBCE | Keep CE fixed initially | Sampled margins differ from validation HR@10 |

**Candidate assessment.** Scores are originality/potential/user alignment/model alignment/difficulty; higher difficulty means harder implementation. Each entry gives a positive and negative reason.

| Idea | Scores | Positive / negative assessment by dimension |
|---|---|---|
| A. Directional recent residual | 4/7/7/6/3 | O: specific combination / established components; P: extensible / sparse transitions; U: recent successors / usefulness unverified; M: supervised separation / cause uncertain; D: small projections / serialization care |
| B. Recency–recurrence gate | 3/6/7/5/5 | O: causal support / familiar gating; P: adaptive evidence / interest lock-in; U: narrow recurrence / novel interests suppressed; M: context filtering / sensitivity unmeasured; D: backbone retained / masking complexity |
| C. Matched-negative gBCE | 2/6/3/8/3 | O: controlled transfer / established loss; P: calibration / CE advantage unknown; U: fewer distractors / no intent mechanism; M: direct competition / sampled proxy; D: local change / sampling cost |

**Selected: A.** It explicitly targets broad relatedness displacing recent narrow interests and persistent demand assumptions that promote related variants. Ordered successor supervision may distinguish useful next choices from symmetric affinity; both benefits remain hypotheses. Its model-facing target is sampled positive–negative inversion, especially in Electronics.

Pool only causal recent embeddings; score through separate source and target projections, with a zero-start residual coefficient. Compare against unchanged SASRec and an otherwise matched symmetric residual before adding gates or changing losses. Select exclusively by pinned four-category macro validation HR@10; preserve all routing, splits, seeds, interfaces, and budget accounting. No new gain is claimed.

References: [1] https://arxiv.org/abs/1808.09781; [2] https://arxiv.org/abs/2311.01056; [3] https://www.ijcai.org/proceedings/2024/0939.pdf

idea.description: Add a zero-initialized directional recent-history scoring residual to each category-specific SASRec. For causal exponentially pooled recent embeddings r_t, use z_t = h_t + alpha A r_t and candidate vector E_i + B E_i. To preserve baseline scores exactly at initialization, implement the score as h_t·E_i + alpha (A r_t)·(B E_i), rather than multiplying the two augmented vectors. Alpha starts at zero; A and B are distinct bias-free projections initialized after the unchanged baseline. Retain the existing explicitly defined uniform multi-negative candidate-set CE objective for the first architecture comparison.
idea.motivation: Two user-facing targets are broad relatedness displacing recent narrow interests and past interaction being interpreted as continuing demand for related variants. A recent source representation prioritizes immediate evidence, while separate source and target projections can learn ordered successor associations rather than only symmetric similarity. Neither mechanism identifies actual ownership, replacement need, compatibility, quantity, or mood. The model-facing target is positive–negative ranking inversion: Electronics has a 0.1596 sampled negative-win rate and −0.4829 lower-tail margin. These measurements motivate a controlled experiment, not a claimed causal diagnosis or validation improvement.
idea.implementation_notes:
Use three observed sequence positions with fixed weights proportional to 0.5^(t-j), including t; exclude padding and renormalize. Use raw tied item embeddings without position embeddings or the encoder input multiplier. Construct A and B after baseline initialization, using a separate initialization RNG context that restores the training RNG state. Initialize both to identity and alpha to zero. The effective residual is initially symmetric but can become asymmetric because the two projection parameters are independent. Put alpha in a no-weight-decay optimizer group with otherwise baseline optimizer settings; preserve existing groups for baseline parameters. Do not normalize after residual fusion. Compare baseline, matched symmetric residual using a shared projection, and directional residual; do not assume supplied historical scores constitute matched comparisons.

Keep DATA_DIR = os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR'], preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42, all four datasets and category routing, unchanged splits, trial-local artifacts, and the SASREC_EPOCHS environment setting with default 200. Do not allocate new search time without subtracting prior consumption from the shared 43,200 GPU-second allowance. Training, checkpoint inspections, diagnostics, debugging, and failures all count. Use only the host's pinned macro validation HR@10 for selection; retain per-category results when supplied. Never reconstruct or modify host candidates, consult hidden tests, or claim unobserved outcomes.

Update the predictor writer with exactly the same module, configuration, projections, alpha, item mappings, and category routing. For the compatibility interface, log2feats can return concatenated features [h_t, alpha*A*r_t]; predict_score must dot these with concatenated candidate representations [E_i, B*E_i]. Keep view.item_emb as the actual shared embedding table and view.model as the actual trained module. Adapt probes to call predict_score rather than assuming feature dimension equals embedding dimension. Preserve DiagnosisProbe(view, device).run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), returning metrics and metric_definitions, and retain user_train, meta_data, and review_data interfaces without fabricating fields. Embedding alignment continues to measure the shared E table, with that limitation stated.

Before training, verify finite empty-window behavior, zero-alpha baseline score equality, suffix invariance of earlier scores, nonzero finite alpha gradients on a nondegenerate example, and score equality after checkpoint reload. Monitor residual/base score contribution and fixed-loader sampled negative-win rates. Keep diagnostic definitions unchanged and treat sensitivity as supplementary. Only public histories, timestamps, titles, and descriptions are admissible; this experiment needs histories alone.
idea.pseudocode:
class DirectionalRecentResidual(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, dim):
        super().__init__()
        self.source = nn.Linear(dim, dim, bias=False)
        self.target = nn.Linear(dim, dim, bias=False)
        nn.init.eye_(self.source.weight)
        nn.init.eye_(self.target.weight)
        self.alpha = nn.Parameter(torch.zeros(()))

    def features(self, baseline_features, sequence, item_emb):
        valid = sequence.ne(0)
        emb = item_emb(sequence).masked_fill(~valid.unsqueeze(-1), 0)
        pooled = torch.zeros_like(emb)
        count = emb.new_zeros(sequence.shape)
        for lag, weight in enumerate((1.0, 0.5, 0.25)):
            if lag >= sequence.size(1):
                break
            if lag == 0:
                pooled = pooled + weight * emb
                count = count + weight * valid.to(emb.dtype)
            else:
                shifted_emb = torch.nn.functional.pad(emb[:, :-lag], (0, 0, lag, 0))
                shifted_valid = torch.nn.functional.pad(valid[:, :-lag], (lag, 0))
                pooled = pooled + weight * shifted_emb
                count = count + weight * shifted_valid.to(emb.dtype)
        pooled = pooled / count.clamp_min(1e-8).unsqueeze(-1)
        residual = self.alpha * self.source(pooled)
        return torch.cat((baseline_features, residual), dim=-1).masked_fill(~valid.unsqueeze(-1), 0)

    def candidates(self, item_ids, item_emb):
        e = item_emb(item_ids)
        return torch.cat((e, self.target(e)), dim=-1)

# Define these methods in the actual trained SASRec module:
# log2feats(sequence): compute original h; return residual.features(h, sequence, item_emb)
# predict_score(features, items): align batch/candidate axes explicitly, then
#     sum(features * residual.candidates(items, item_emb), dim=-1)
# Use these same methods for training, diagnostics, and generated prediction code.
# Score one positive and the unchanged K uniform negatives at each valid position.
# loss = cross_entropy(concat(positive_score, negative_scores), target_index_zero)
# Keep the inherited sampler's eligibility rules explicit and unchanged across arms.
# Select checkpoints only using host-provided four-category macro validation HR@10.
# Symmetric control: share source and target projection parameters; otherwise match settings.

originality.positive: Combines a controlled zero-start residual with recent-source, directional target scoring in a small extension of the supplied baseline.
originality.negative: Recent pooling, asymmetric factorization, and gated residuals are established components; this is an incremental experimental combination.

future_potential.positive: A successful matched comparison could support later work on context-dependent transition direction and separate calibration experiments.
future_potential.negative: Sparse successor observations and symmetric popularity shortcuts may limit benefits; useful complements and replacement needs remain unobserved.

code_difficulty.positive: Requires two small projections, one scalar, short-window pooling, and no graph construction or external data.
code_difficulty.negative: The concatenated scoring interface requires synchronized training, diagnostic adapters, checkpoint loading, and predictor generation.

related_work.title: Self-Attentive Sequential Recommendation
contributions: Provides the causal self-attention backbone and next-item scoring baseline.
limitations: Does not establish compatibility, ownership, or immediate practical demand from interaction histories.

related_work.title: TiCoSeRec
contributions: The supplied search summary describes weighted directed transition information integrated into sequential recommendation, motivating ordered scoring.
limitations: Does not establish benefits for this lightweight residual or the pinned RecHarness protocol.
Observed transition direction is behavioral association rather than verified complementarity.

related_work.title: gSASRec
contributions: Motivates controlled comparisons of negative count and generalized BCE calibration.
limitations: Evidence against BCE does not establish superiority over candidate-set CE in this task.
An objective change alone provides no explicit mechanism for recent intent or useful successors.
